comment: Cursor/VS Code rendering map: how each tool named in policy.json becomes concrete
editor configuration. This is the only place extension IDs and code-action IDs appear.
A second IDE gets its own render.<ide>.json — policy.json never changes for it.
Tools whose policy authority is 'repo' are listed for reference but are never bound
as editor.defaultFormatter; the repo's own config governs those languages.

vscode-json.note: Built-in JSON language features. Biome's Cursor/VS Code extension does not register a formatter for the jsonc language id (settings.json, tsconfig.json, …).

prettier.note: Markdown only in biome_default. The built-in Markdown Language Features extension does not register a formatter.
